scope: Proposition 2.2 (Common cap and Green data) of the manuscript “Smooth anisotropic uniqueness in the Calderón problem from one boundary patch” (preprints/Smooth-Anisotropic-Uniqueness-in-the-Calderon-Problem-from-One-Boundary-Patch-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 365 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1ec46ed64206d12d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 2.1, there are compact connected smooth extensions (Me j , ge j ) of (M, gj) and an identified connected open exterior cap E on which the extended metrics agree. The cap is attached through a nonempty open set P0 ⋐ Γ. The extended zero-Dirichlet Green kernels satisfy G1(x, y) = G2(x, y), x, y ∈ E, x ̸= y. For every F ∈ C∞ c (E), the two extended zero-Dirichlet solutions with source F agree on E.
